entries.name: restore_actor_update_ostrich
entries.reason: Historical actor_prey.c already implements the Ostrich state/render/RNG structure with explicit correct base strides. It is a separate source-only test provider, absent from main libraries. Direct wiring is not exact: random_wait performs two complete random_tick calls, publishing/reloading RNG/index between them; native state8 keeps cached words/index across its two31-step phases and publishes its final index after the second history write. Entry source captures speed/group/building before native reset/counter phases. Original image() has numerically corresponding heading normalization, but omits intermediate native global stores and fresh-read phases.
entries.recommendation: Describe as adaptation/correction of the existing ordinary implementation, with new production wiring and native-order repair. Do not claim a previously absent ordinary state-machine algorithm or claim unchanged old body is byte-correct.

entries.name: restore_actor_update_service_state
entries.reason: Complete existing state1/2/4/5/default algorithm uses correct explicit volatile BYTE/WORD/DWORD accesses and388/264 strides. It is not a blank frame/decompiler body. However state is loaded after speed/home, unlike native, and targetX is loaded after state2 publication, unlike the native cached pre-store value. Query argument load order is also not explicit in the old C expression.
entries.recommendation: Treat as reuse of an existing ordinary algorithm plus explicit native cache/read/store-phase corrections, not as an independently absent algorithm. Keep current reconstructed behavior; this read-only report does not request reverting native-order fixes.

entries.source_problem: DAT_00bca2d0 is unsigned BYTE, while native reads signed/full DWORD dimensions. Its home and building coordinate typed-array expressions additionally double/quadruple the native offsets.
The initial signed/full DWORD gate is declared BYTE; state/cooldown DWORD-macro arrays also use four times the native actor byte stride.
Native forms offset row*96 bytes (LEA3row,SHL5). Source adds row*96 DWORD elements, i.e. row*384 bytes. Its BYTE gridbase and output-table scaled pointer additions also differ.
Native phase is BYTE at base+actor*388. Source DWORD-macro array indexed by actor*388 addresses base+actor*1552 and stores DWORD. This is more than a volatile/cache refinement.

Native distance scratch publication is DWORD; the existing macro is BYTE. Owner group uses DWORD-array index actor*194, addressing base+actor*776 instead of signed WORD at base+actor*388; group restriction pointer also scales4.
Native originWORD is at base+actor*388. Source DWORD indexingactor*194 reaches base+actor*776 before casting low16. dx publication is also BYTE instead of DWORD.
